Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 19:50:14 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] s390/entry: Scrub r12 register on kernel entry

Before commit f33f2d4c7c80 ("s390/bp: remove TIF_ISOLATE_BP"),
all entry handlers loaded r12 with the current task pointer
(lg %r12,__LC_CURRENT) for use by the BPENTER/BPEXIT macros. That
commit removed TIF_ISOLATE_BP, dropping both the branch prediction
macros and the r12 load, but did not add r12 to the register clearing
sequence.

Add the missing xgr %r12,%r12 to make the register scrub consistent
across all entry points.

Fixes: f33f2d4c7c80 ("s390/bp: remove TIF_ISOLATE_BP")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Ilya Leoshkevich <iii@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Vasily Gorbik <gor@linux.ibm.com>

diff --git a/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S b/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S
index 4873fe9d891b..689d253e1afc 100644
--- a/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S
+++ b/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S
@@ -271,6 +271,7 @@ SYM_CODE_START(system_call)
 	xgr	%r9,%r9
 	xgr	%r10,%r10
 	xgr	%r11,%r11
+	xgr	%r12,%r12

 	xgr	%r6,%r6
 	xgr	%r7,%r7
 	xgr	%r10,%r10
+	xgr	%r12,%r12

2.34.1

The patch adds the missing `xgr %r12,%r12` instruction to clear the `r12` register at three kernel entry points in `arch/s390/kernel/entry.S`. This ensures all saved or uninitialized register contents are scrubbed consistently before kernel code runs, closing a security gap introduced when the previous `r12` load (for branch prediction macros) was removed.

### File modifications

- **`arch/s390/kernel/entry.S`** – `system_call` entry:
  - Added `xgr %r12,%r12` (clear r12) after clearing other registers (r9, r10, r11).

- **`arch/s390/kernel/entry.S`** – Macro-based syscall entry (e.g., `SYM_CODE_START` block):
  - Added `xgr %r12,%r12` after clearing r6, r7, r10.

- **`arch/s390/kernel/entry.S`** – `mcck_int_handler` (machine check) entry:
  - Added `xgr %r12,%r12` after clearing r6, r7, r10.

### Relationships between modifications

All three modifications serve the same purpose: restoring the register scrubbing that was inadvertently omitted when the `TIF_ISOLATE_BP` mechanism and its associated `r12` load were removed. The `r12` register is no longer loaded with the current task pointer, but it may contain sensitive or stale data from userspace or previous kernel activity. By adding the clear instruction at every primary entry point (syscall, exception/interrupt, and machine check), the patch ensures that `r12` is zeroed out uniformly, maintaining the security invariant that all general-purpose registers are sanitized early in the kernel entry path.
